Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise, source-of-truth answers we use in inbound RFIs. I’ve attached a short retention matrix and a deletion-flow diagram for your security team to include with the questionnaire. If anything needs a DPA-level commitment we can escalate.

1) Data residency (hosted API)
- Customer-visible content (prompts + generated outputs): stored in the region selected during account provisioning (region lock) when that option is chosen. For customers on the default plan we host in our primary US region (us-east-1) and process in a GDPR-compliant manner; optional EU region pinning available with an addendum.
- Metadata (routing/metrics) may be replicated to secondary regions for observability; replication is encrypted in transit and at rest.

2) Default retention windows (hosted API)
- Generated content (chat responses & request payloads): retained for 90 days by default.
- Embeddings & vector indices created by the service: retained for 30 days by default unless customer persists externally via our export API.
- Operational logs (request/response logs used for billing/troubleshooting): retained for 90 days; aggregated telemetry for platform health is retained longer (365 days) in an aggregated/anonymized form.
- Backups & daily snapshots: short-term snapshots are kept for 7 days (hot backups) and then moved to a 30-day warm retention tier used for disaster recovery; these snapshots are encrypted and access-controlled.

3) Deletion and purge behaviour
- Tenant-level deletion request: we accept an authenticated request (via Console or Support ticket). Once requested we mark the tenant for purge and initiate a deletion workflow within 24 hours. Active objects (data in primary stores and indices) are removed within the first 72 hours.
- Backups/snapshots: purge from warm/cold backup tiers occurs on the next scheduled lifecycle pass; worst-case timeframe to remove from all backups is 30 days after the deletion sweep begins. We provide a certificate of deletion once the run completes.
- Cache behavior (prefix/KV cache): KV caches are ephemeral (default TTL 1 hour) and do not survive tenant deletion; any active entries are invalidated as part of the deletion job. We do keep short-lived diagnostic caches for up to 24 hours to aid rollback — these are included in the 72-hour active deletion window.

4) Encryption & key management
- All customer content is encrypted at rest using AES-256. Keys are managed by our KMS; we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS for customers who require them (enterprise add-on).

5) Audit evidence & attestation
- We can provide deletion audit logs (time-stamped job events and the unique purge job id) and a signed certificate of deletion. Our SOC 2 reports and supporting artifacts are available under NDA; we’ve included the retention matrix for quick reference.

Attachments: redwood_retention_matrix_v1.pdf, hostedapi_deletion_flow_diagram.png

Let me know if you want these numbers tightened for a contractual clause (example: reduce backup purge window to 7 days for an addendum). Happy to hop on a call with your compliance team.

Regards,
Karthik

Hi Emma — quick answers:

1) Accelerated backup purge
- We can offer an accelerated backup purge SLA (7 days) as a contractual addendum under our Dedicated/Enterprise package. For hosted API customers on standard plans we keep the 30-day maximum to balance DR and operational economics. The accelerated purge requires additional orchestration and a dedicated runbook to ensure no snapshot remnants in replicated cold stores — hence the addendum.

2) Embeddings TTL and per-tenant config
- Embeddings created via the managed embeddings endpoint support an optional TTL parameter at creation; if absent default is 30 days. For enterprise accounts we can configure a per-tenant default TTL and offer hard-expiry enforcement.

Operationally, when an embedding expires it is removed from the primary index and marked for pruning; physical deletion in background completes within 24–72 hours depending on index compaction schedules.

Next steps: Marissa, can you confirm whether we should draft an addendum template for Orchid (7-day backup purge + tenant-level embedding hard-expiry)?

Thanks,
Karthik
